title: The bare necessities of a physically reasonable mathematical model for quantum theory
abstract: The physical foundation of the mathematical formalism of quantum theory is still an iffy mystery. Here it is presumed that a physically reasonable mathematical model needs only three basic features. The first one are the transition probabilities, which are so typical of quantum theory. The other two constitute a variation of the postulate that continuous reversible dynamical processes exist and act transitively on the underlying space. One class of mathematical models with these features arises from the atomic JBW factors, which include the atomic von Neumann factors and become identical with the Jordan matrix algebras, when the dimension is finite. A further model is known, on which the exceptional Lie group E6 acts transitively. Interestingly, E6 is sometimes considered a candidate for internal symmetries in particle physics, but many familiar features of quantum theory get lost in this case (particularly the general existence of post-measurement states). The paper concludes with some open issues, concerning this problem and the classification of the mathematical structures with the three features.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the fundamental mathematical requirements for a consistent theory of quantum mechanics by analyzing its transition probability spaces. It proposes that three key features—transition probabilities, continuous dynamics, and topological homogeneity—must be present in any physically valid model. The work connects these abstract requirements to known algebraic structures like JBW factors and exceptional Lie groups.
main_problem: The core problem is determining the minimal set of mathematical features required for a physically reasonable formulation of quantum theory, as its foundational basis remains mysterious.
main_result: The paper suggests that such models must possess transition probabilities, continuous reversible dynamics acting transitively, and topological homogeneity. These constraints lead to structures related to atomic JBW factors or specific exceptional Lie group actions like E6.
method: The analysis involves abstract mathematical characterization of 'transition probability spaces' (E, P), examining their algebraic structure via Jordan algebras, and analyzing symmetry groups acting on these spaces.
model_or_system: The model is the general formalism of quantum theory itself, analyzed through its transition probabilities. Specific mathematical realizations include atomic JBW factors, von Neumann factors, and models associated with convex sets or exceptional Lie groups like E6.
key_observables: Transition probabilities P(e1|e2), capacity (m), connectedness, and homogeneity of the state space.
important_parameters: The dimension of the underlying algebra, the structure group acting on the space (e.g., SO(n) or E6).
main_assumptions: It assumes that a physically reasonable model must satisfy three specific mathematical criteria: transition probabilities, continuous reversible dynamics, and topological homogeneity.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the necessary features (transition probabilities + dynamics/topology) and then reviewing known mathematical structures—such as JBW factors and models based on convex sets—that satisfy these criteria. It concludes by listing open classification problems.
why_interesting: This work tackles the foundational axioms of quantum mechanics, which underpins all applications in AMO physics. Understanding the necessary mathematical structure provides deep insight into what physical principles must govern measurement and evolution.
